gallery.title: File:Håndkle, Bjørn Østring, monogram (HL-senteret, 2016-10-06).jpg
gallery.description:
Håndkle med Bjørn Østrings monogram. Da Amalie Laksov kom tilbake til leiligheten sin i Dunkersgate 4 i Oslo etter krigen var den overtatt av familien Østring. De hadde brodert monogrammet sitt på Laksovs håndkle.
På utstilling hos Senter for studier av Holocaust og livssynsminoriteter.
categories: Center for Studies of the Holocaust and Religious Minorities

gallery.filename: Hvem er Hvem i Jødeverden samt fortegnelse over fremmedes forretninger i Norge 4. utgave Nationalt Tidsskrift Mikal Sylten Oslo 1941 Norwegian Anti-Semitic address list booklet Holocaust exhibition HL-senteret Norway 2021 9607.jpg
gallery.title: File:Hvem er Hvem i Jødeverden samt fortegnelse over fremmedes forretninger i Norge 4. utgave Nationalt Tidsskrift Mikal Sylten Oslo 1941 Norwegian Anti-Semitic address list booklet Holocaust exhibition HL-senteret Norway 2021 9607.jpg
gallery.description:
Photo taken at the Norwegian Center for Holocaust and Minority Studies (Norwegian: HL-senteret) in Oslo, showing items from the permanent exhibition on antisemitism, the Holocaust, etc.:
Hvem er Hvem i Jødeverden ("Who's Who in the Jewish World")
Pamphlet cataloguing Jews or presumed Jews in Norway, written and published by the Norwergian antisemite Mikal Sylten (1873–1964) in 1941. Sylten was used as a consultant for the nazi authorities during the German occupation of Norway during the Second World War.
categories: Center for Studies of the Holocaust and Religious Minorities

gallery.filename: HL-SENTERET Bygdøy Oslo NORWAY 2021-11-22 Senter for studier av Holocaust og livssynsminoriteter Norwegian Center for Holocaust and Minority Studies Villa Grande building (1917 WW2 Quisling residence) park driveway etc wide IMG 9321.jpg
gallery.title: File:HL-SENTERET Bygdøy Oslo NORWAY 2021-11-22 Senter for studier av Holocaust og livssynsminoriteter Norwegian Center for Holocaust and Minority Studies Villa Grande building (1917 WW2 Quisling residence) park driveway etc wide IMG 9321.jpg
gallery.description:
Wide angle photo of the Villa Grande, a property on Bygdøy in Oslo, Norway, taken in November 2021.
The building was constructed in 1917, but the site was later redeveloped for use as the fascist leader Quisling’s “Führer residence” during the Second World War in German-occupied Norway. In 2005, the Center for Studies of the Holocaust and Religious Minorities (Norwegian: HL-senteret) moved into the building.
categories: Center for Studies of the Holocaust and Religious Minorities
